subject: dsa
title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
summary: dp[i] is the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends at index i. For each i, look at every earlier index holding a smaller value and extend its best run by one. The answer is the largest dp value.
problem: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of an array (elements need not be contiguous).

steps.caption: dp[i] = length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at index i. Every element on its own is a run of length 1.
dp[0] = 1 (just 3). dp[1] = 1, since no value left of 1 is smaller than it.
dp[2]: values left of 4 that are smaller are 3 and 1; the best dp among them is 1, so dp[2] = 1 + 1 = 2.
dp[3]: only 1 is smaller than 2 to its left, and dp[1] = 1, so dp[3] = 1 + 1 = 2.
dp[4]: 4 and 2 are both smaller than 5; the best dp among them is 2, so dp[4] = 1 + 2 = 3.
The largest dp value is 3, so the longest increasing subsequence has length 3 — for example 1, 4, 5 or 1, 2, 5.
